question:
A 18-year-old female presents to the clinic with low back pain. She was recently seen in the emergency
department after falling off a ladder at which time a full workup, including a CT spine series, was
negative for acute injury. She states the worst of the pain is improved but she continues to have
residual discomfort. She describes the pain as achy, and it worsens when she lies down. On
osteopathic structural examination, there is a right posterior transverse process palpated at the level of
the spinous process of T10, which becomes more pronounced when the spine is extended. The
paraspinal musculature is hypertonic and tender from T9–T12. Which of the following is the correct
diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) T11 FRRSR (B) T10 FRRSR (C) T10 FRLSL (D) T9 ERRSR (E) T9
FRRSR (F) T11 ERRSR (G) T10 ERRSR (H) T11 FRLSL (I) T12 ERRSR (J) T12 FRRSR
 A. T11 FRRSR
B. T9 ERRSR
C. T10 FRRSR
D. T9 FRRSR
E. T11 FRLSL
F. T10 FRLSL
G. T12 ERRSR
H. T10 ERRSR
I. T11 ERRSR
J. T12 FRRSR
